title: Restore default SIRead granularity to cut predicate-lock bookkeeping
configuration_cause: Incumbent forces coarsest SIRead granularity (max_pred_locks_per_page=0, max_pred_locks_per_relation=0), which promotes every page/relation predicate to relation-level SIRead locks; with 5 terminals and 3.5M GetUserTweets calls this inflates lock bookkeeping (locks_total p95 340, max 460) without any lock waits (lock_waiting_backends max 0).
mechanism: The incumbent sits at the coarsest SIRead extreme (page=0, relation=0). Coarser granularity means each scanned page promotes to a relation-level SIRead lock, so per-transaction lock bookkeeping grows with the number of relations touched rather than being capped per page. Restoring PostgreSQL defaults (page=2, relation=-2) keeps page-level SIRead locks up to 2 per page and lets relation-level promotion follow the default fraction of the per-txn budget, reducing lock churn per GetUserTweets while leaving the generous 8192 per-txn budget intact. Since lock_waiting_backends is already 0, the win is bookkeeping/CPU, not wait removal.
query_effect: GetUserTweets (87.6% of terminal capacity) should see slightly lower per-call lock bookkeeping; no plan change expected.
expected_tps_effect: Small positive: reduced lock bookkeeping frees CPU on the dominant transaction class; magnitude bounded because lock waits are already zero.
expected_latency_effect: GetUserTweets p99 flat-to-slightly-down; no regression expected on other classes.

predictions.rationale: Default page/relation caps stop every page from promoting to relation-level SIRead locks, lowering total lock count p95.
Less per-call lock bookkeeping trims the dominant transaction's tail.
Freed CPU on the 87.6%-capacity transaction class raises completed-transaction goodput.
No lock waits exist today; granularity change must not introduce them.

alternatives.statement: If the residual bottleneck is WAL commit-path queueing rather than lock bookkeeping, restoring SIRead defaults will leave locks_total.p95 and GetUserTweets p99 unchanged while wal_waiting_backends.p95 stays at 1.
If promotion churn is budget-bound rather than granularity-bound, the default caps will not reduce locks_total.p95 and only a larger max_pred_locks_per_transaction would.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent's coarsest-granularity extreme (page=0, relation=0) maximizes relation-level SIRead promotion; defaults cap page-level locks at 2 and let relation promotion follow the default fraction, cutting bookkeeping on the dominant transaction without touching the already-zero lock-wait regime.

nodes.label: Default SIRead granularity caps page-level locks and reduces relation-level promotion churn

knob_changes.numerical_basis: PostgreSQL default 2, inside allowed [0,256]; reverses incumbent 0 extreme toward default midpoint.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: page-level predicate-lock granularity cap; 2 keeps up to 2 SIRead locks per page before promotion instead of promoting every page

knob_changes.numerical_basis: PostgreSQL default -2, inside allowed [-2,4096]; reverses incumbent 0 extreme toward default fraction of per-txn budget.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: relation-level predicate-lock granularity cap; -2 uses the default fraction of the per-txn SIRead budget instead of forcing relation-level promotion

cross_domain_requirements: memory_storage owns the WAL commit-path bundle; wal_waiting_backends.p95=1 persists and is not addressed here
